title: Data-order length weighting: every epoch presents each training record once plus a second copy of every 6-line record (the cap-6 maximum), on the 153-claude width-384 Lean incumbent (9,557,760 params)
description: Data-order (presentation) change, no new idea ID (closest backlog family: curricula, which Robbie put in scope 2026-09-25): the token-budget epoch gains a second copy of each of the ~30.8k 6-line records, so 6-line proofs get 2x the gradient passes of every other length while every record stays in play. The metric and every RL target are >= 7-line proofs, so pretraining that weights the longest available proofs more should hand RL a sampler whose round-1 7+ line proofs are better formed, raising round-1 targets solved and the final count.
hypothesis: Round-1 sampling on 7-14 line targets is the metric's strongest predictor (153, 157, 159), and it is an extrapolation from the pretraining length range (2-6 lines, uniform). The 6-line records are the only ones whose long-range structure (many cited premises, late lines citing early ones, a long prefix before QED) resembles the targets, but they are 1/5 of records and are presented as often as 2-line proofs. Doubling their presentation moves the model's per-token fit toward the long-proof regime (more epochs on it: ~2x vs ~1x-rate for others) without dropping anything, so the T=0.8 sampler should produce fewer malformed/unterminated long proofs (Lean parse failures 15-16% of samples on 153) and solve more round-1 targets. Unlike 157-fable3's ascending first epoch (a transient order effect that hurt round-1) this is a stationary reweighting through the whole run. Risks: (a) 6-line proofs are memorized faster (they already overfit at ~4 epochs; now ~8 passes), which could narrow the sampler; (b) short proofs get ~17% fewer passes in the same wall-clock, possibly weakening basic rule use; (c) RL's own fine-tuning on solved 7+ line targets may wash the effect out after round 1.
expected_delta: -35 to +35 theorems at >=7 (3-seed mean), central +3; keep needs > 687.00. Mechanism predictions: steps 4,300-4,700 (153: 4,540/4,479/4,489; step content unchanged, ~18.4k padded tokens), batches per epoch ~1,380-1,420 (153: 1,132), 'epochs' stat (records_seen / 153,966) 3.8-4.2 with each 6-line record seen ~6.5-7x vs ~3.3x for other lengths; n_params 9,557,760; final main val loss (all lengths) 0.080-0.095 (153: 0.088/0.087/0.089); held-out greedy 0.955-0.975; round-1 RL targets solved 700-860 (153: 766/747/694), round-4 RL-solved 1,140-1,220 (153: 1,157/1,168/1,191). Falsifier: round-1 targets solved at or below 153's on every seed means the reweighting did not improve the long-proof sampler, and any metric change is noise.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, unchanged from 151-claude except width; PeriLNBlock now replaces the fork Block's 4*D fc1/fc2 with Linear(D, D_FF)/Linear(D_FF, D), D_FF = 1280 (same as 151's 4*320)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: none vs 153-claude: identical model, init, optimizer, schedule, MTP; only the epoch composition changes (data.order).
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,557,760 (CPU check with fork 51604b3, vocab 107; bench_pretrain on an A40 reported the same; per Peri-LN block 1,579,136 = qkv 443,520 + proj 147,840 + fc1 492,800 + fc2 491,904 + 4 LayerNorms 3,072; emb + head 82,176; ln_f 768). MTP module (pretraining only, never registered on the model, dropped at handoff as since 136-fable): 1,875,584; pretraining trains 11,433,344 in total, so unlike 151 the total is over 10M if the discarded MTP module were counted; the harness caps the handed-off model's parameters (9.56M), which is what RL and eval use
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 1280), then load state; the MTP module is not saved and not needed for inference
arch.kv_cache: unchanged (caches[0] holds key positions); CPU check cached vs full forward max abs logit diff 1.4e-6 at width 384

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (384,768) input proj) join Muon and its LayerNorms/biases join AdamW (unchanged from 151)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock, unchanged from 129/151: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 30 Muon matrices as in 148/151 (CPU check: muon_step runs over all 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (384,768): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are 9,557,760

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, warmup, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged. The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: CHANGED vs 153-claude: each epoch = a fresh random permutation of the 153,966 training records (val slice excluded) PLUS a second copy of every 6-line record (~30,800 more, +20% records per epoch, ~+25% tokens), then stably sorted by token length, cut into TOK_BUDGET 18,432-token batches, batch order shuffled (148-fable's token-budget batching unchanged). REPEAT_LINES = 6. No record dropped or filtered; data lengths are uniform (30,996-30,999 records each for 2..6 lines).

config.init: unchanged rule from 148/151: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 384; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40 (probe, not evidence): 695 steps in 60.3 s = 11.53 steps/s (148-fable's shape: 13.2), peak 7.42 GB, n_params 9,557,760, sampling 179 samples/s (148: 186)
